sentences.text: Camarasaurus was a bulky sauropod dinosaur that lived in North America during the Late Jurassic. It is characterized by a proportionally wide rib cage, making it relatively heavy compared to other members of its group.
Like the contemporary Brachiosaurus, this animal had an enlarged external nostril resulting in an arched forehead.
The name Morosaurus was once used to refer to the animal, highlighting its small brain size relative to its massive body.
Because little was known about the skull and most reptiles were assumed to be carnivorous, early reconstructions depicted Camarasaurus with a hypothetical skull bearing long, sharp teeth.
Some Camarasaurus specimens represent embryos, while others reached an estimated age of 40 years, making them among the oldest known individual dinosaurs.
A Camarasaurus embryo fossil measured 37 mm in bone length, suggesting a total body length of just over 1 meter and a body weight of 7.5 kg.
Modern evidence from anatomy and trackways suggests that Camarasaurus held its entire tail off the ground.
In 25% of Camarasaurus specimens, the foremost tail vertebrae were fused together, a condition caused by ossified tendons rather than direct bone fusion.
A 2016 study estimated that Camarasaurus had a bite force almost four times stronger than that of Diplodocus, reaching up to 1978 newtons at the back of its tooth row.
In 2002, researchers used oxygen isotope thermometry to analyze bone apatite in a Camarasaurus specimen to estimate body temperatures.
The largest species, Camarasaurus supremus, reached a maximum length of 23 meters and an estimated weight of 47 tons.

The genus Camarasaurus was described by Edward Drinker Cope in 1877 during the 'Bone Wars', a rivalry between paleontologists Othniel Charles Marsh and Edward Drinker Cope that spurred fossil discoveries in the late 19th century.
More than 530 specimens of Camarasaurus have been found in the Morrison Formation of the western United States.
Camarasaurus was a herbivore that likely fed on vegetation at heights between 2 and 5 meters. It was likely a selective feeder that browsed at these heights.
Camarasaurus was discovered during the 'Bone Wars', a rivalry between paleontologists Othniel Charles Marsh and Edward Drinker Cope that spurred fossil discoveries in the late 19th century.
In 1877, Cope believed that Camarasaurus was capable of and accustomed to moving on land.
A 2007 study by Paul Sereno suggested that the head of Camarasaurus was habitually tilted down by about 15 degrees, based on inner ear anatomy.
Large bite marks on Camarasaurus fossils likely indicate attacks by Torvosaurus or Allosaurus.
A Camarasaurus pelvis recovered from Dinosaur National Monument in Utah shows bite marks attributed to Allosaurus.
Large Camarasaurus individuals were likely immune from predation by theropods like Torvosaurus.
The strength of its teeth suggests Camarasaurus likely ate tougher plant material than Diplodocus, which had thinner teeth.

A fossil record of two adults and a 12.2-meter-long juvenile found together in Wyoming was excavated by the University of Kansas and the Center for Biodiversity during field expeditions in 1997 and 1998.
Senter (2026) presented evidence of a limited range of motion in the fingers of Camarasaurus.

Carpenter, Ikejiri, and Wilson (2026) studied the postcranial anatomy of two immature Camarasaurus lentus specimens from Dinosaur National Monument, interpreting them as sequential ontogenetic stages to reveal morphological variability.
In 2026, researchers found that Camarasaurus finger anatomy made previously proposed walking postures impossible.
The type species of the genus Camarasaurus is Camarasaurus supremus.
Camarasaurus is classified as a member of the sauropod group Macronaria.
Since 1998, Camarasaurus has been classified as a basal member of the sauropod group Macronaria.
Some paleontologists debate the classification of Camarasaurus, suggesting it belongs in the family Camarasauridae alongside genera like Tehuelchesaurus and Lourinhasaurus.
Henry Fairfield Osborn implied in 1898 that several genera, including Apatosaurus and Brontosaurus, were synonyms of Cope's Camarasaurus.
Camarasaurus lived during the Late Jurassic, from the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian ages, between 155 and 143 million years ago.
Camarasaurus supremus primarily lived during the Tithonian stage at the top of the Morrison Formation.
